factors.name: Coherent Revision Ratchet Drift
factors.description: Computes recent five-bar fractional EPS and revenue consensus revisions, then retains them only when they agree in sign with the preceding fifteen-bar revision interval. The cross-sectional rank is high for confirmed positive analyst-revision ratchets and low for confirmed negative ratchets.
factors.trading_idea: Repeated same-direction changes in EPS and revenue consensus identify a ratcheting analyst-information process rather than a one-off estimate maintenance update. When a fresh revision continues the direction established over the prior few weeks, analysts are likely incorporating dispersed evidence sequentially and institutional portfolios adjust with delay, producing short-horizon drift. The edge should persist because estimate production, committee approval, and benchmarked portfolio implementation are staggered; it is falsified if consecutive same-sign consensus changes do not outperform isolated revisions over the next six bars.

factors.name: Consensus Margin Revision Wedge
factors.description: Ranks the difference between percentage changes in consensus EPS estimates and consensus revenue estimates over a trailing 42-bar interval. High values indicate EPS forecasts improving materially more than sales forecasts, consistent with an unpriced expected margin improvement.
factors.trading_idea: Analysts often revise revenue and EPS forecasts through different information channels: a positive EPS revision that is large relative to the accompanying revenue revision implies an improving expected margin, pricing, or cost outlook rather than merely stronger nominal demand. Margin-information is harder for investors to verify immediately and is incorporated gradually as subsequent disclosures validate the operational improvement, while portfolio managers commonly react first to headline sales revisions. The edge should therefore persist because the signal isolates a forecast-composition shock rather than generic estimate momentum; it is falsified if high-wedge firms do not subsequently exhibit stronger realized profitability or do not outperform over the next six bars.

factors.name: Cash-Funded Net Payout Capacity
factors.description: On newly updated quarterly financing observations, ranks firms by executed net share repurchases scaled by market capitalization, augmented by free-cash-flow yield and penalized for net debt issuance. The signal is zero between filing updates, isolating delayed assimilation of sustainable versus externally financed shareholder payout.
factors.trading_idea: Newly reported net buybacks financed by free cash flow rather than debt are a credible signal that management has private confidence in durable earnings capacity, and they mechanically increase per-share claim growth that analysts often incorporate only gradually. Conversely, equity issuance or debt-financed payout signals financing pressure and should precede weaker returns. This is falsifiable: among new quarterly filings, a portfolio sorted on cash-funded net-payout capacity should have positive six-day residual IC even after controlling for earnings-surprise and short-run price-response factors; the edge persists because financing-source reconciliation is less salient than headline earnings and requires combining separate cash-flow and financing statements.

factors.name: Fear-State Stale Surprise Diffusion
factors.description: Ranks fresh positive EPS surprises with stale estimates and muted report-day price response, conditional on prior market-fear/idiosyncratic drawdown, balance-sheet resilience, and a coherent positive price-volume cascade. The event impulse decays over six bars and is cleared when the EPS estimate updates.
factors.trading_idea: The child treats broad-fear capitulation as a state variable that makes prior selling less informative, but only trades it when a fresh positive earnings surprise remains unincorporated by stale consensus and the report-day price response is still below the fundamental implication. It then requires the announcement to reignite a pre-existing positive return-volume execution cascade, identifying constrained investors beginning a delayed re-risking process rather than a mechanical panic bounce. The interaction carries edge because capitulation alone mixes genuine deterioration with forced selling, while stale-surprise drift alone does not distinguish a quietly underreacted report from one backed by persistent institutional demand.

factors.name: Coherent Surprise Response Gap
factors.description: At newly observed earnings reports, computes the signed average of normalized EPS and revenue surprises and subtracts the stock's volatility-scaled announcement-day return. The resulting coherent-news response gap is carried causally for six post-report bars and ranked cross-sectionally.
factors.trading_idea: Earnings information diffuses gradually when both earnings and revenue surprises point in the same direction but the contemporaneous price response is small relative to the fundamental news. The child goes long positive coherent surprises that received too little immediate price confirmation and short negative coherent surprises that were insufficiently discounted, expressing the gap over the following six sessions. The edge should persist because interpreting cross-channel earnings releases and reallocating institutional portfolios takes longer than reacting to a headline; it is falsified if response-gap portfolios have no positive 6-bar return spread after controlling for the signed surprise itself.

factors.name: Forecast Operating-Leverage Translation
factors.description: The signal combines a trailing revenue-estimate revision with a causal quarterly operating-leverage proxy, measured as the change in operating income divided by the absolute change in revenue over roughly one fiscal quarter. It ranks firms whose positive demand revisions should translate most efficiently into operating-profit upgrades.
factors.trading_idea: Revenue-consensus upgrades should be more valuable when a firm's recently reported incremental operating margin is high: fixed-cost businesses translate additional expected sales into disproportionately larger future earnings. Investors and headline-driven trading often process revenue revisions as comparable demand news across firms, while the accounting-based operating-leverage mapping is slower to incorporate and difficult to arbitrage without bearing earnings-event risk. The hypothesis is falsified if firms with high revenue revisions and high reported incremental operating margins neither receive subsequent earnings upgrades nor outperform over the next six bars.

factors.name: Debt-Financed EPS Engineering Unwind
factors.description: Compute the cross-sectional wedge between epsGrowth and netIncomeGrowth, rewarding a negative score when apparent EPS acceleration is accompanied by negative sharesGrowth, negative or weak freeCashFlow, and positive debtGrowth. Normalize the accounting components by cross-sectional ranks and suppress names with missing or implausible quarterly accounting values.
factors.trading_idea: Investors often reward reported per-share earnings growth without immediately separating operating profit growth from mechanically lower share counts. The signal identifies firms whose EPS growth materially exceeds net-income growth while buybacks coincide with weak free-cash-flow support and rising debt, a combination consistent with financial engineering rather than improving economics. The edge should be falsified if these firms do not subsequently underperform otherwise comparable firms after the disclosure becomes incorporated; the natural opposite side is headline-oriented earnings and buyback demand.

factors.name: Unassimilated Consensus Revision Gap
factors.description: Ranks each stock's 21-bar EPS-consensus revision and subtracts the rank of its sector-neutral five-bar return. The signal is active only when consensus has actually changed, isolating revisions not yet reflected in relative prices.
factors.trading_idea: Analyst consensus revisions contain gradually disseminated fundamental information, but the six-bar drift should be strongest when the stock's sector-relative price response has lagged the revision rather than already incorporating it. The child therefore buys positive estimate revisions with weak relative price acknowledgement and shorts negative revisions whose prices remain unusually resilient. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on a recent revision, forward returns should increase monotonically with the gap between revision direction and contemporaneous sector-relative return; the edge can persist because revisions arrive discretely across analysts and institutional investors face staggered mandate, research, and trading constraints.

factors.name: Funding-Constrained Receivables Drift
factors.description: The signal identifies recent increases in receivables divided by revenue, carries the disclosure shock forward with a causal exponential decay, and weights it by short-term-debt dependence net of cash reserves. Higher values represent worsening cash conversion at financially fragile firms and are predicted to precede lower returns.
factors.trading_idea: A newly reported increase in receivables relative to revenue indicates that reported sales are being converted into cash more slowly, creating a funding-liquidity shock that is especially consequential for firms reliant on short-term debt and with little cash buffer. Investors often initially focus on reported revenue while the financing implication is incorporated gradually through credit, inventory, and equity-risk reassessment over subsequent sessions. The hypothesis is falsified if firms with a fresh receivables-intensity deterioration and high funding fragility do not underperform otherwise similar industry peers over the next six days; the edge can persist because interpreting filing-level working-capital changes and their financing consequences is costly and less salient than headline earnings.

factors.name: Peer Cash-Cycle Muted-Reaction Fragility
factors.description: Scores fresh joint increases in receivables/revenue and inventory/revenue only when leave-one-out industry receivables stress is elevated, short-term funding fragility is high, and the current three-day price response is small relative to trailing volatility. The industry-neutralized score is high for firms expected to underperform over the next six daily bars.
factors.trading_idea: A firm's receivables-and-inventory deterioration is most informative when recent peer disclosures already establish a common customer-credit or demand shock, but the firm's own price has not yet reacted materially to its filing. Funding-fragile firms cannot absorb the resulting cash-conversion pressure, so muted initial price response represents an attention-limited underreaction rather than resilience. Neither parent alone identifies this disclosure-to-price assimilation gap: peer confirmation validates that the event is systemic, while the muted-response state selects the cases where the validated shock remains unpriced.

factors.name: Funding-Gated Absorbed Sell Reversal
factors.description: The signal identifies coherent signed price-volume pressure with unusually low range impact, then reverses absorbed selling only when a volatility-scaled market drawdown coincides with sector-relative working-capital funding fragility.
factors.trading_idea: During a systemic drawdown, persistent low-impact selling in firms with weak cash buffers, high leverage, and slow inventory conversion is more likely to be forced funding-driven liquidation than informed repricing. Liquidity providers can temporarily absorb this supply, but constrained arbitrage capital prevents immediate correction; once the selling schedule eases, the absorbed inventory produces a short-horizon rebound. The interaction matters because balance-sheet fragility identifies the economic origin of the flow, while the absorbed-flow signature identifies names where that stress has actually reached the market but has not yet cleared.

factors.name: Peer Hawkes Contagion Underreaction
factors.description: Computes a Hawkes-style exponentially decayed intensity of volatility-standardized, volume-weighted signed returns for each stock. It compares each stock's intensity with the leave-one-out intensity of its sector peers, activates only when peer excitation is strong, and sector-demeans the resulting contagion-underreaction score.
factors.trading_idea: Institutional order flow often propagates across economically related names over several daily bars: a large, signed, volume-supported move in peer firms raises the conditional probability of subsequent same-direction flow in a lagging constituent. The factor approximates this cross-excitation with an exponentially decayed signed-flow intensity, then buys names whose own intensity lags a strongly positive leave-one-out sector intensity and shorts the converse. The edge should persist because execution is fragmented across funds, liquidity differs by constituent, and sector ETF/index demand is not instantaneously transmitted into every stock; it is falsified if peer-flow gaps do not predict same-direction six-bar returns after sector demeaning.

factors.name: Broad Peer-Flow Absorption Repair
factors.description: Computes leave-one-out industry breadth of abnormal downside-volume events, then favors names experiencing the same event while closing high in their daily range. The final score is sector-neutralized so it identifies relative absorption rather than broad sector beta.
factors.trading_idea: Broad, contemporaneous downside-volume participation within an industry is more consistent with basket, ETF, or risk-budget liquidation than with a firm-specific information event. A focal stock that also trades under downside pressure but closes near the top of its range has revealed latent demand capable of absorbing that non-informational supply, so its price should repair over the next six sessions. The edge persists because investors cannot cheaply distinguish forced common flow from informed selling in real time, while liquidity providers need time and balance-sheet capacity to replenish inventory; it is falsified if high-close-location names fail to outperform weak absorbers during equally broad peer sell episodes.

factors.name: Common-Shock Quality Defense (jitter) (jitter)
factors.description: Measure a causal market synchrony state from the cross-sectional share of stocks moving in the same direction and the first-principal-component share of recent return variation. During elevated synchrony, rank firms by a defensive quality composite of roe, roic, grossMargin, freeCashFlowYield, cashRatio, debtToEquity, and debtToAssets; shrink the score toward zero outside the regime.
factors.trading_idea: When daily returns become unusually synchronized across the market, a common risk shock dominates firm-specific price discovery and capital reallocates toward balance-sheet quality. In that state, profitable cash-rich firms with conservative leverage should outperform fragile firms over the following week because passive de-risking and mandate-constrained investors cannot immediately rebalance every exposure. This is a cross-sectional implementation of factor timing: it should fail if high return synchrony does not raise the subsequent quality-minus-fragility spread, despite the signal being active only during common-shock regimes.

factors.name: Surprise-Rupture Opposing-Flow Release
factors.description: At earnings events, the factor scales coherent EPS and revenue surprises by each firm's prior event-surprise magnitudes and carries the signed joint rupture forward briefly. It goes long positive ruptures facing persistent negative volume-tail excitation and short negative ruptures facing persistent positive excitation.
factors.trading_idea: A coherent, historically unusual joint EPS-and-revenue surprise establishes an idiosyncratic common-information shock, but its six-day pricing effect is strongest when the immediate high-participation order-flow cascade runs against the news. Such opposing flow is consistent with liquidity-constrained rebalancing, stale-position unwinds, or slow institutional model revision absorbing the shock rather than disproving it. The interaction has edge neither parent has alone: surprise novelty identifies when a flow imbalance is informative rather than generic, while persistent opposite-signed flow identifies delayed shock propagation rather than an already-completed earnings drift.

factors.name: Disclosed Float Overhang Capacity
factors.description: Detects fresh public updates to net stock issuance and share-count growth, then estimates the corporate float shock relative to market capitalization. It scales the decaying signed shock by market-cap-to-dollar-volume turnover days, ranking buyback overhangs positively and issuance overhangs negatively.
factors.trading_idea: Newly disclosed net equity issuance or buybacks alter the effective public float and force gradual portfolio rebalancing by benchmarked, capacity-constrained investors. The price effect should be negative after issuance and positive after repurchases, especially where the implied float adjustment is large relative to the stock's normal dollar-turnover capacity; the signal decays because the demand imbalance is gradually absorbed. This is falsifiable: conditional on a fresh share-count or net-issuance disclosure, subsequent 6-bar returns should be more negative for issuance and more positive for repurchase in names with longer turnover-implied absorption times. The edge can persist because disclosure-driven ownership rebalancing is costly and staggered, while arbitrageurs face the same liquidity and borrow constraints that slow the adjustment.

factors.name: Conditional Impact Copula Information Residual
factors.description: Fits a causal rolling conditional model of absolute log returns on log volume surprise, then ranks the signed positive residual: price moves larger than their volume-implied expectation receive the sign of the move. The signal deliberately distinguishes information-rich displacement from normal high-volume mechanical impact.
factors.trading_idea: Routine liquidity-motivated trading produces a relatively stable conditional relationship between daily volume surprise and absolute return. A return that is unusually large even after conditioning on contemporaneous activity is a break in that price-volume coupling: it is more likely to reflect information arriving through dispersed investors than a mechanically completed liquidity trade, so its signed direction should continue over the next six sessions. This is falsified if signed conditional-impact residuals reverse after controlling for volume surprise; the edge can persist because daily volume cannot reveal the private-information content, investor heterogeneity, or gradual institutional response behind an abnormal displacement.

factors.name: Sparse Liquidity Vacuum Repair
factors.description: Ranks the expected six-day reversal of a signed return that is unusually large relative to its trailing volatility while contemporaneous volume is below its own causal baseline. High values are long recent negative sparse-liquidity shocks and short recent positive sparse-liquidity shocks.
factors.trading_idea: The parent's negative realized IC indicates that unusually large signed displacement relative to activity is more often a temporary liquidity-vacuum move than dispersed information. This child explicitly isolates shocks occurring on abnormally sparse participation: a large return with below-normal volume is likely caused by a transient absence of resting liquidity, dealer inventory imbalance, or a brief withdrawal of counterparties, which is repaired gradually as liquidity returns over the following week. The hypothesis is falsified if low-participation excess-impact shocks continue in their original direction, rather than reversing, at the fixed six-day horizon; the effect can persist because daily volume does not reveal latent depth or the speed of inventory replenishment.

factors.name: Volume-Marked Directional Excitation Pressure (jitter)
factors.description: Define signed flow marks from close-to-close return sign times abnormal volume, retain tail events relative to each stock's rolling volume distribution, and apply an exponentially decayed event kernel. The factor is positive when recent positive marked events have a higher inferred self-excitation intensity than negative events, with a penalty for sign alternation and excessive intraday-range reversal.
factors.trading_idea: Daily signed return-volume shocks can act as coarse observations of latent buy and sell order-flow events. Repeated same-sign, unusually high-participation events over a decaying window indicate a self-exciting metaorder or information-diffusion process whose impact is not fully completed, whereas alternating signs imply that excitation is being absorbed by opposing liquidity. The effect should fail when elevated volume is not directionally clustered, which distinguishes persistent order-flow pressure from generic high-volume noise.

factors.name: Persistent Absorption Range Compression (jitter)
factors.description: Computes abnormal signed close-location volume pressure, requires it to persist across a trailing 12-bar event clock, and amplifies it only when recent normalized high-low ranges are compressed relative to the stock’s own trailing range baseline. The output is sector-neutral cross-sectional rank, long persistent absorbed buy pressure and short persistent absorbed sell pressure.
factors.trading_idea: Repeated abnormal directional trading with unusually compressed intraday ranges indicates a latent metaorder being absorbed by replenishing liquidity rather than immediately incorporated into price. Unlike the parent’s short-lived acceleration signal, this child requires sustained directional participation across many days and uses range compression as evidence that dealer inventory capacity is being consumed, implying that subsequent price adjustment should occur as absorption capacity weakens. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on equally persistent signed-volume pressure, forward returns should be substantially stronger when realized ranges are compressed than when the same pressure already produces wide-range price discovery; the edge can persist because institutional execution schedules and liquidity replenishment are not directly observable from daily bars.

factors.name: Fear-Onset Financing State Relay
factors.description: Builds a financing-resilience score from liquidity, cash generation, leverage, and interest coverage, then adds a decayed innovation component reflecting recent changes in that cross-sectional state. The score is activated only after a broad downside shock with unusually negative market breadth.
factors.trading_idea: During an abrupt broad-market fear episode, investors and risk models tend to extrapolate stale financing-risk classifications rather than immediately incorporating newly reported improvements in liquidity, cash generation, leverage, and debt-service capacity. The signal therefore favors firms with both high current financing resilience and recently improving relative resilience, because these firms should receive delayed defensive reallocation over the following week. The edge should disappear in calm markets, and it should weaken if one controls for the most recent reported financing-state change; it persists against arbitrage because accounting availability is discrete while institutional risk-budget and mandate reallocations occur gradually after stress begins.

factors.name: Industry Delayed Information Elasticity
factors.description: Computes leave-one-out industry peer returns, estimates a causal rolling beta of each stock's three-day return on peer returns lagged three bars, and applies that elasticity to the current standardized peer-return innovation. The final score is industry-neutralized so it selects relative delayed responders rather than simply taking an industry directional bet.
factors.trading_idea: Industry news is not incorporated simultaneously across firms: specialist coverage, heterogeneous investor attention, and staggered portfolio rebalancing make some names reliable delayed responders to their peers' information shocks. The factor estimates each stock's trailing sensitivity to an industry-peer return observed three bars earlier, then buys high-sensitivity followers after a fresh positive peer innovation and shorts them after a negative innovation. This is falsifiable if a stock's estimated lagged peer-response coefficient does not positively interact with subsequent returns following standardized peer shocks; the edge can persist because the relevant leader-follower mapping is heterogeneous and time-varying rather than a static industry-momentum basket.

factors.name: Leave-One-Out Industry Impulse Lag
factors.description: Computes a volatility-normalized leave-one-out industry return gap, weighted by positive industry excess return and positive-peer breadth. High values identify lagging stocks in broadly advancing industries.
factors.trading_idea: Information and institutional sector reallocations diffuse unevenly across firms: a broad positive industry impulse is incorporated first in liquid or salient peers, while temporarily lagging members catch up over subsequent sessions. The child goes long stocks whose own three-day return lags a leave-one-out industry-peer return, but only insofar as the peer move is positive relative to the market and broadly shared across the industry. This should persist because portfolio-manager attention, peer-comparison workflows, and constrained rebalancing operate with delay; it is falsifiable because the premium should disappear when the peer impulse is nonpositive or concentrated in only a small fraction of peers.

factors.name: Consensus Revision Whipsaw Correction
factors.description: Ranks the magnitude of a fresh EPS-estimate change only when it reverses the preceding estimate change and price has initially moved in the latest revision’s direction. The signal shorts positive revision whipsaws and buys negative revision whipsaws.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s negative six-day result is consistent with short-lived extrapolation of unstable consensus changes rather than delayed incorporation of peer-confirmed information. When an EPS-consensus revision reverses a recent revision and the stock has already moved in the direction of the latest revision, the newest estimate change is likely an analyst-model whipsaw rather than durable fundamental news; the initial price response should unwind over the following week. This edge can persist because consensus feeds aggregate asynchronous analyst edits and many investors mechanically treat the latest directional change as information, while identifying rapid reversals requires maintaining event history rather than reacting to the current revision alone. It is falsified if price-confirmed revision reversals continue in the direction of the latest estimate change over six bars rather than mean-revert.

factors.name: Bad-News Cascade Drift
factors.description: Computes an exponentially decayed bad-earnings-news impulse and interacts it with acceleration in a marked downside-return intensity process. Higher values indicate active bad-news-driven downside cascades and predict lower forward returns.
factors.trading_idea: Negative earnings surprises can trigger an asymmetric cascade of sell orders when contemporaneous downside return innovations are self-exciting rather than isolated. The signal identifies names where a freshly released negative earnings surprise coincides with accelerating downside-shock intensity, predicting further six-day underperformance while analyst revisions, margin deleveraging, and liquidity-provider risk repricing occur. This edge can persist because fundamental-news interpretation and institutional risk reduction are slower than mechanical arbitrage; it is falsified if high-score names reverse or have no residual underperformance after controlling for the earnings surprise alone.

factors.name: Downside Innovation Cluster Continuation
factors.description: Measures the excess of a fast exponentially weighted intensity of volatility-scaled negative returns over its slower pre-event baseline, multiplied by the density of prior downside shocks. High values identify recurrent, self-exciting downside innovation clusters.
factors.trading_idea: Clusters of downside volatility innovations proxy for self-exciting sell pressure: margin calls, risk-limit reductions, and liquidity-provider withdrawal cause one negative shock to raise the probability of further negative shocks. The signal explicitly suppresses isolated bad-news moves and activates only when abnormal negative returns recur, so it targets endogenous order-flow persistence rather than generic volatility. The edge should persist because constrained sellers and dealer inventory adjustment cannot be instantaneously arbitraged away; it is falsified if high cluster scores do not predict relatively lower six-bar returns after conditioning on recent return and volatility.

factors.name: Idiosyncratic Shock Relaxation Phase
factors.description: Ranks the signed five-day price displacement only when a recent idiosyncratic range-volatility shock is decaying and dollar-volume capacity has recovered from its local trough. Long candidates are negative shocks entering replenishment; positive shocks entering the same phase are short candidates.
factors.trading_idea: The parent mixes the immediate shock with its later repair phase, which is consistent with its stronger 1-3 bar and 12-bar results but weak 6-bar result. This child explicitly enters only after an idiosyncratic range-volatility shock has begun to relax and trading capacity has replenished, identifying the gradual inventory-transfer phase in which liquidity providers can unwind positions and prices continue to normalize over roughly a week. The edge should persist because replenishment and inventory redistribution are constrained by dealer balance sheets and by investors' staggered execution rather than being instantaneously arbitraged. It is falsified if, conditional on equally large idiosyncratic shocks, names with declining range stress and recovering dollar volume do not have more signed 6-day reversal than names whose stress remains elevated.

factors.name: Downside Range Innovation Absorption Release
factors.description: Ranks stocks with a recent, conditionally unusual idiosyncratic downside/range shock whose close recovers materially from the intraday low. Expected downside movement and range are estimated with slow causal exponential baselines, while event relevance decays over roughly one trading week.
factors.trading_idea: A downside return normally raises expected volatility through the leverage and bad-news asymmetry, but an unusually large downside range relative to the stock's own pre-shock downside and range state is more likely to reflect a temporary liquidity vacuum. When the close finishes well above the intraday low, the selling shock has been absorbed rather than continuously repriced, so inventory replenishment and volatility mean reversion should support returns over the following week. This is falsified if stocks with large conditional downside-range innovations and high close-location do not outperform after controlling for contemporaneous idiosyncratic return and realized range; the edge can persist because liquidity replenishment and forced-sale completion are slower than the daily shock that creates the dislocation.

factors.name: Endogenous Sell-Cluster Relaxation
factors.description: Computes a volume-marked, market-adjusted downside-event intensity using a short exponential decay and compares it with a slower background intensity. High scores identify names where an elevated sell cluster has recently decelerated, consistent with exhaustion of endogenous liquidation pressure.
factors.trading_idea: Downside returns accompanied by unusual participation can form self-exciting liquidation clusters: prior selling raises volatility, triggers risk limits, and attracts further mechanically motivated sales. The child goes long only as the exponentially decayed sell-pressure intensity begins to fall from an elevated level relative to its slower background, indicating that the endogenous cascade is exhausting rather than that negative information is still arriving. This is falsified if the post-extinction signal has no positive six-day return after controlling for recent idiosyncratic return, realized volatility, and relative volume; the edge can persist because latent liquidation completion is difficult to distinguish from informed selling in daily data and liquidity providers require time to replenish inventory.

factors.name: Funding-Fragility Downside Variance Innovation
factors.description: Computes the fast-versus-slow innovation in downside semivariance of returns residualized against the same-day cross-sectional market move, then weights it by a point-in-time balance-sheet fragility score based on debt-to-equity and cash ratio. Higher values denote an idiosyncratic bad-news volatility shock in a financially constrained firm.
factors.trading_idea: An abrupt increase in idiosyncratic downside semivariance is more informative when a firm has both high leverage and a thin cash liquidity buffer: negative shocks then raise collateral, refinancing, and risk-capacity concerns rather than merely reflecting a transitory market move. Constrained holders and lenders reduce exposure gradually, so high fragility-weighted downside-volatility innovation should predict negative six-bar returns. The edge can persist because balance-sheet constraints and the distinction between systematic versus name-specific bad-news volatility are not directly tradable, while short-sale risk and crash exposure limit immediate arbitrage. This is falsified if downside-volatility innovations have no more negative subsequent return among cash-poor, levered firms than among well-funded firms.

factors.name: Bad-News Thin-Book Persistence
factors.description: Ranks the severity of freshly released negative EPS surprises multiplied by accelerating downside-return intensity and persistent negative residual endpoint pressure on thin-book range shocks. High values identify negative-news sell cascades still clearing through depleted closing-auction liquidity.
factors.trading_idea: A negative earnings surprise alone mixes genuine information with oversold, already-absorbed liquidation, which explains why Parent A's unconditional cascade direction was unstable. This child only activates when the surprise-driven downside cascade is expressed through repeated closes near the low of unusually wide, low-turnover bars: a thin-book auction state indicating that sell demand remains unexecuted rather than fully incorporated into price. The interaction has edge because Parent B's endpoint state becomes informative when anchored to a fresh fundamental catalyst, while Parent A's bad-news cascade becomes a continuation signal only when liquidity withdrawal prevents immediate price discovery.

factors.name: Downside Kernel Release
factors.description: Computes fast and slow exponentially weighted intensities of volatility-scaled negative returns, weighting events more heavily when volume confirms participation. It ranks the sector-neutral difference between slow and fast downside-event intensity, scaled by the name's trailing intensity baseline.
factors.trading_idea: Forced deleveraging and stop-loss activity create clustered negative-return events whose intensity decays only gradually after the marginal seller has exhausted inventory. The signal estimates fast and slow exponential kernels of volume-confirmed downside shocks: a slow kernel above the fast kernel identifies a recently intense sell cascade that is now decelerating, while the reverse identifies fresh downside ignition. The falsifiable hypothesis is that names with the largest sector-relative kernel-decay state outperform names with fresh downside acceleration over the next six sessions; the edge can persist because constrained sellers and liquidity providers unwind inventory over multiple days rather than instantaneously.

factors.name: News-Synchrony Forced-Flow Conversion (jitter)
factors.description: The signal detects newly available industry-relative earnings or revenue surprise, measures sector-wide incidence of abnormal price-impact and return stress, and scores the surprise-to-price conversion gap only when the stock moves opposite to its news on high-impact, low-turnover bars. Non-event or non-stress observations are neutral.
factors.trading_idea: Fundamental surprises are normally informative, but their initial price response is unreliable when a sector-wide liquidity shock forces correlated trading and temporarily overwhelms name-specific information. The child buys positive-surprise names that suffer an idiosyncratic sector-relative selloff during synchronized thin-liquidity stress, and shorts negative-surprise names experiencing the symmetric forced uplift. Parent A identifies overshoots without knowing whether the displaced name has fundamental support, while Parent B identifies delayed news conversion without distinguishing a name-level thin book from a sector-wide forced-flow episode; their interaction isolates fundamentally anchored dislocations likely to repair within the fixed six-bar horizon.

factors.name: Earnings-Disambiguated Liquidity Repair (jitter)
factors.description: The signal combines a sector-wide liquidity-stress and persistent negative-arrival repair score with an earnings-anchor tail classifier. Industry return and estimate-revision concordance convert fresh extreme post-report displacements into a signed information-continuation leg and attenuate the forced-flow rebound leg for confirmed bad-news events.
factors.trading_idea: Sector-synchronous, high-volume sell-arrival clusters are usually mechanical deleveraging shocks and tend to repair when a name is unusually weak relative to its sector. However, Parent B's realized negative IC indicates that peer-concordant tail moves from a fresh earnings anchor are informational continuation events rather than reversals: peer agreement validates gradual incorporation of a heavy-tailed belief shock. The child therefore buys forced-selling residuals only after discounting names whose downside is earnings-anchored and industry-confirmed, while allowing peer-confirmed positive and negative earnings tails to retain their directional continuation component.

factors.name: Quality Update Price-Assimilation Gap
factors.description: Ranks fresh cross-sectional changes in ROIC, income quality, and gross margin, then interacts them with the opposite of each stock's recent industry-relative return. It is long firms with improving reported quality whose prices have lagged peers and short firms with deteriorating quality whose prices have outperformed peers.
factors.trading_idea: The parent suggests that fundamental-quality information is useful, but its complex factor-premium timing layer is likely noisy and vulnerable to multiple-testing deflation. This child isolates a slower mechanism: investors extrapolate recent industry-relative price performance and underreact to newly disclosed improvements or deteriorations in operational quality, especially when the price move initially points the other way. The edge should persist because quarterly accounting updates are costly to interpret and are incorporated gradually by investors focused on headline price action; it is falsified if fresh quality updates no longer predict six-day returns conditional on prior industry-relative performance.

factors.name: Nonlinear Downside Coskew Compensation
factors.description: Computes each stock's residual return after removing trailing linear market beta, then measures its negative loading on squared market losses observed only in the market's lower-tail days. Higher values identify stocks with greater nonlinear downside-tail exposure and therefore a predicted compensation premium.
factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk implies that investors require compensation for stocks whose losses become disproportionately severe in broad market downside-tail states, beyond their ordinary linear market beta. This child estimates that nonlinear downside exposure from trailing daily returns and ranks stocks by their residual loss loading during market-tail observations. The premium can persist because crash-state risk is difficult for arbitrageurs to warehouse and is especially unattractive to investors with leveraged or consumption-sensitive liabilities; the hypothesis is falsified if high residual downside-tail loading does not precede higher six-bar returns after controlling for ordinary beta.

factors.name: Tail-Cluster Resilient Liquidity Release
factors.description: After a clustered market-tail regime is detected, ranks accelerating close-near-low abnormal-volume selling and scales it by cross-sectional balance-sheet resilience. High scores identify financially resilient names whose systemic deleveraging pressure is most likely to reverse over the next week.
factors.trading_idea: Clustered broad left-tail days proxy for rare high-marginal-utility consumption states in which investors reduce risk mechanically, while close-near-low abnormal-volume selling identifies the names receiving the immediate liquidity shock. The child goes long the strongest downside-pressure names only when they have resilient financing capacity, because selling of cash-rich, low-leverage firms in a systemic tail episode is more likely delegated risk-budget liquidation than new solvency information. Fragile firms are deliberately excluded because identical order-flow pressure is more likely to reveal genuine refinancing risk; this interaction distinguishes temporary forced-flow overshoots from fundamental deterioration, which neither parent can isolate alone.

factors.name: Consumption-Tail Semibeta De-Risking
factors.description: Computes each stock's recent change in conditional beta to negative market returns, scales it by current aggregate downside-tail stress, and penalizes fragile cash-ratio names more heavily. Higher scores identify firms with stable or falling downside exposure during a tail-risk regime.
factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth states are proxied by market downside-semivariance bursts, when marginal investors become unusually sensitive to assets whose returns have recently acquired greater downside exposure. A rising conditional downside beta should trigger short-horizon de-risking most strongly for firms with weak cash-liquidity buffers, because their equity is more exposed to financing and consumption-tail states. The edge should persist because tail-risk sensitivity is estimated noisily and portfolio-risk reallocations occur gradually; it is falsified if downside-beta innovations do not predict relatively negative six-day returns specifically during elevated market downside-semivariance regimes after conditioning on cash liquidity.

factors.name: Consumption-Tail Amplification Premium
factors.description: Computes each stock's leave-one-out market beta on market-tail days and subtracts its ordinary trailing beta. The factor ranks stocks by this nonlinear downside-tail exposure, long high tail-amplification names and short low tail-amplification names.
factors.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth risk implies that the relevant priced exposure is not ordinary market beta but the additional sensitivity of a stock specifically on aggregate downside-tail days. Stocks whose returns co-crash more than their normal beta predicts should require higher expected returns as compensation for losses when marginal utility is highest; this premium can persist because arbitraging it requires bearing concentrated crash risk and financing drawdowns. The hypothesis is falsifiable: after controlling for ordinary market beta, forward six-bar returns should increase monotonically with estimated downside-tail beta amplification, and the relationship should be weakest for names without statistically sufficient tail observations.

factors.name: Idiosyncratic Downside Branching Pressure
factors.description: Computes a daily Hawkes-style branching-pressure proxy: a standardized idiosyncratic downside innovation multiplied by exponentially decayed prior downside-event intensity relative to its own slow background event rate. High values identify fresh negative shocks embedded in an unusually self-exciting downside cluster.
factors.trading_idea: The parent’s useful feature is conditional downside continuation, but this child replaces balance-sheet fragility with an endogenous-order-flow mechanism. A fresh idiosyncratic negative return is more likely to continue when it arrives after a short sequence of prior downside innovations, because forced selling, stop-loss execution, and dealer inventory reduction create self-exciting sell pressure rather than an isolated information shock. The edge should persist because arbitrageurs face uncertain cascade duration and adverse selection during the selling episode; it is falsified if equally large idiosyncratic losses have the same six-day forward return regardless of their pre-shock downside-excitation intensity.

factors.name: Reported Buyback Execution Clock
factors.description: Computes a decaying signal from fresh quarterly share-repurchase disclosures, scaled by trailing 20-day dollar volume to estimate the number of normal trading days represented by the disclosed repurchase flow. Long names with recently confirmed, turnover-large buybacks.
factors.trading_idea: A newly reported, large share-repurchase outlay relative to the stock's normal dollar turnover reveals an active corporate demand program whose likely execution horizon is long compared with one trading day. Unlike a generic value or reversal signal, the relevant state variable is the inferred execution clock: large disclosed buyback capacity combined with limited market turnover implies persistent, price-insensitive demand over the next several sessions. This is falsifiable if fresh repurchase disclosures with high repurchase-to-ADV ratios do not outperform equally recent filings with little or no repurchase activity; the effect can persist because exact corporate execution schedules are opaque, institutions face front-running and mandate constraints, and the demand is mechanically distributed through time rather than immediately incorporated into price.

factors.name: Earnings Turnover-Impedance Resolution
factors.description: Ranks fresh EPS-surprise events by signed surprise magnitude times a turnover-impedance measure. Impedance is high when volume is far above its trailing baseline while the contemporaneous return is small relative to trailing volatility.
factors.trading_idea: A fresh earnings surprise accompanied by unusually high turnover but an abnormally small same-day price displacement represents a disagreement auction: informed investors trade against liquidity suppliers and slower discretionary investors without immediately moving the daily midpoint. The direction of the reported surprise should subsequently dominate as the temporary opposing inventory is unwound and investors who require time to interpret the report update positions. This is falsified if high-impedance surprise events do not deliver stronger six-day returns in the direction of the surprise than equally sized surprise events with immediate price displacement; the edge can persist because this conditional state is infrequent and cannot be identified from the surprise or volume alone.

factors.name: Recovery Bounce Sell-Schedule Continuation
factors.description: The signal identifies a fresh downside-range shock that closes strongly off its low, then amplifies it only when prior downside shocks have elevated a causally estimated exponential arrival intensity and volume is unusually high. Higher values indicate likely continuation of an unfinished sell schedule and are expected to precede lower returns.
factors.trading_idea: A close near the daily high after a large downside excursion is not necessarily genuine absorption: when it occurs amid an already clustered sequence of downside shocks and unusually high participation, it can be a temporary dealer-facilitated bounce during an unfinished institutional sell program. Execution constraints, benchmarked liquidation schedules, and limited displayed depth prevent such flow from being immediately arbitraged away, so the residual selling pressure should depress returns over the next six sessions. This hypothesis is falsified if high-scoring recovery bounces in high-participation downside clusters subsequently outperform rather than underperform the cross-section.

factors.name: Uniform Sell Participation Backlog
factors.description: Computes volume-normalized downside pressure and ranks the product of its trailing mean and directional coherence. High values represent persistent, regularly sized sell participation rather than isolated downside shocks.
factors.trading_idea: A scheduled institutional sell program produces repeated downside bars with unusually stable volume participation, unlike a one-off information shock or panic liquidation whose daily pressure is irregular. The signal identifies names with both high recent downside participation and high temporal coherence of that participation, indicating that an execution backlog is likely still active and should predict negative six-day returns. This is falsifiable: conditional on the same cumulative downside pressure, high-coherence names should underperform low-coherence names; the edge persists because daily bars do not reveal the parent order's remaining quantity or execution schedule, while trading against it entails inventory and timing risk.
